In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Raman bands at 250 cm −1 and 860 cm − 1 are due to the oxymethylene groups in the poly (oxyethylene).
the bands at 260 and 280 cm −1 are assigned to the C−O−C deformation modes in the polymer chain and are not influenced by the salt concentration in the polymer electrolyte.
the Raman spectra of the polymer electrolytes show that the oxymethylene-linked polymer chains are not involved in the conduction mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bands in the 250–310 and ca. 800–900 cm −1 regions are due to the presence of the ether groups in the polyether.
the 250–310 and 860 cm − 1 bands are related to the formation of ion pairs in the polymer electrolytes.
the Raman spectra of these polymer electrolyte systems are consistent with the formation of ion pairs and ion clusters in these systems, and the formation of a salt-rich phase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 860 cm − 1 band is sensitive to salt concentration and is useful for monitoring the degree of salt dissociation.
